reason: The response vectors and exact binomial-mixture arithmetic match the counterexample, but ceilingBeta is only a deterministic mixture functional. There is no jointly modeled affected indicator, assignment, affirmative-response population, or identification of that functional with the observable conditional-mean beta. No numerical power guarantee is asserted.

The corrected response increments and both exact mixture formulas are retained for every rho in [0,1], but not their conditional-observable-mean identification in a joint population. The narrative Monte Carlo power assertion is omitted; claims.json itself says it has no exact formal counterpart.

The same sixteen-atom population supplies the substantive counterexamples, with positive empty-cell mass, zero-completion covariances, the occupied n=4 product-variance discrepancy, and random treatment counts. The full population and moment tables, second conditional-variance equality, and general conditional-binomial and missing-mass assertions are absent; four displayed missing-mass numbers are only scalar arithmetic. One population-cell mean, m10=5/6, is retained.

All main corrected conditional-variance identities and the covariance order and limit are represented. The conditional-binomial block is asserted only at sample sizes n>=2, whereas the canonical count law also covers n=0,1. The identity K=n(1-ybar) is not separately asserted. Occupied-cell and fibre conditionals have positive denominators under the displayed assumptions.

The eight-atom valid null model and its control, treated-plus-one, and treated-minus-one probabilities at zero refute the printed comparison. The full conditional law tables, disjoint supports, numerical nondegeneracy summaries, and all-threshold corrected identities are not asserted.

Exactly the formal distributional conclusion under Assumptions 1-3 and positive affirmative-cell probabilities, with all real thresholds and both equivalent shift identities. Equality of point probabilities determines the finite count distributions. FiniteLaw is a valid representation of the joint law of the bounded counts and binary variables.

The first sixteen-atom example has precisely Assumptions 1,2,4, delta=0, beta=2 and failed joint treatment independence, so it refutes the printed exhaustive diagnosis. The second eight-atom example, numerical tables, potential-response independence assertions, and explicit factorization discrepancy are omitted.

The positive-cell premises, baseline-composition decomposition, beta=1 under Assumptions 1-3, three-alternative contrapositive, and conditional treatment-independence failure diagnosis exactly match the stated formal content. No extra nondegeneracy premise is introduced.

The ordered 128-atom model, independent fair assignments, influence identities and moment matrix, correlated Gaussian limit, Fisher limit, integrability, variance>20 and unequal-law conclusion match the counterexample. The additional finite numerical summaries and explicit marginal-limit, correlation and h-variance formulas are omitted. Completions only affect events whose probabilities tend to zero.

The complete formal sufficient-premise theorem is represented: common iid respondent law, per-list Assumptions 1-4, joint assignment independence, conditional and unconditional cross-influence cancellation, independent normal and uniform limits, and the chi-square-ten Fisher limit. The empirical numbers are explicitly designated nonformal in claims.json. The full joint premise is satisfiable; a 128-atom shared-outcome, independent-assignment model witnesses it.

Parts (a),(b),(e) and asymptotic Wald coverage match the canonical corrected identities and inference. Empty subgroup means and unavailable whole variances are completed by zero, and the normal-quantile set is explicitly required to be nonempty and bounded below; these are disclosed changes of presentation, with the quantile conditions automatic for 0<alpha<1. Source correction to the initial claim-stage reading: the 2015 published PDF, printed p.49 (PDF p.7), explicitly has n times estimated Var[muHat] on the left of the plug-in display, so Defs/Part2.lean:53-55 correctly divides the bracket by n. I initially consulted the earlier arXiv/PMC manuscript, which lacks that n. This is a cited version misreading, not a change based on record.json. Source: https://alexandercoppock.com/aronow_etal_2015.pdf#page=7 . Part (d) has no independent mathematical content, as claims.json itself specifies.
